chunks: Nor can I think that the Hour (of Doom) will come, And even if I am brought back to my Lord, I will surely find a better place there than this.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the certainty of the Hour and the betterment of the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This verse, spoken by Pharaoh's minister Asiya in Surah Ghafir or often associated with the believer of the family of Pharaoh in Surah Al-Kahf, expresses confident anticipation of the Resurrection (Qiyamah) and the superiority of the Hereafter. In Shia exegesis, it underscores the certainty of divine justice and the believer's hope for a better return to their Lord, contrasting worldly transience with eternal bliss.
